There are no written procedures for production and process controls designed to assure that the drug products have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess.
Written production and process control procedures are not followed in the execution of production and process control functions.
Records kept for each different labeling and packaging material shipment fail to include results of examination or testing and a statement of whether the shipment was accepted or rejected.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.
Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.
Time limits are not established when appropriate for the completion of each production phase to assure the quality of the drug product.
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile are not written.

citations.short: Validation lacking for sterile drug products
citations.long: Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile do not include validation of the sterilization process.

citations.short: Strict control not exercised over labeling issued
citations.long: Strict control is not exercised over labeling issued for use in drug product labeling operations.
Test procedures relative to appropriate laboratory testing for pyrogens are not followed.

citations.short: Written records kept in individual logs
citations.long: Written records of major equipment cleaning, maintenance, and use are not included in individual equipment logs.
